answer: A mechanism that actually bites: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because grove only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any knoll approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
